Stated Claim / Post Context:
Police launch investigation into death of Ex on the Beach star Pala Negara's newborn son after home birth 20 days past due date as grieving mother tells the Mail: 'We did everything right'

Police have launched an investigation into the death of her son. Now, Pala tells the Mail what happened, why she feels let down and why she insists 'we did everything right'.

Actual Article Body:
By JONICA BRAY, SENIOR NEWS REPORTER, AUSTRALIA

Published:  01:15 AEDT, 28 October 2026   |  Updated:  01:30 AEDT, 28 October 2026

NSW Police have launched an investigation into the circumstances surrounding the death of former Ex on the Beach star Pala Negara's baby, who died just hours after being born.

The 38-year-old Australian-Balinese model gave birth to her son, whom she named Harmony Hunter, on August 28 at home in Possum Creek, northern NSW, 20 days after his August 8 due date.

But the home birth took a devastating turn when complications saw both mother and baby rushed to Lismore Hospital before being transferred by a NeoRESQ helicopter across the state border to Gold Coast University Hospital.

Despite desperate efforts by medical teams to save him, Harmony died at 8pm that evening.

Ms Negara first announced the tragedy in a social media post alongside her partner, Byron Bay hairdresser Chris Hunter, in September.

Now, the Daily Mail can reveal that officers attached to the Tweed and Byron Police District have 'commenced an investigation following the death of a newborn baby in the state's north'.

'Police were notified after the baby was born in Possum Creek, about 15km west of Byron Bay, about 4.30am on Friday 28 August 2026, and subsequently died at a Gold Coast Hospital later that day,' the police spokesman added.

'A report will be prepared for the information of the Coroner.'

Former Ex on the Beach star Pala Negara announced the tragic death of her child in a social media post alongside her partner, Byron Bay hairdresser Chris Hunter, in September

NSW Police have launched an investigation into the circumstances surrounding the death of Pala Negara's baby. Speaking to the Mail on Tuesday, Ms Negara said she felt 'really let down with what happened with Harmony' after registering with a local home birth program

Speaking to the Mail via phone on Tuesday, Ms Negara said she was registered with a local home birth program provided through Byron Central Hospital.

She claimed that she felt 'really let down with what happened with Harmony', adding: 'We did everything right, we were under the Medicare system and I had my 41-week scan and everything was fine.'

In further correspondence via email, Ms Negara claimed that 'at 41 weeks and six days, I was advised by text that care through the program would end because of its gestational limit'.

Ms Negara said Harmony was later born on August 28 after she went into spontaneous labour in the early hours.

'I understand a rare silent placental abruption occurred during delivery and was identified only afterwards. Paramedics were called and, to my recollection, arrived approximately 40 minutes later.

'Harmony survived for 16 hours and passed away at Gold Coast University Hospital with the Queensland coroner's autopsy findings cause of death due to hypoxic-ischaemic encephalopathy (HIE).'

HIE is a brain injury caused by reduced oxygen (hypoxia) and restricted blood flow (ischaemia) to a newborn's brain before, during, or shortly after birth.

'Alongside our devastating grief, I am receiving counselling and recovering from postpartum haemorrhage,' Ms Negara added.

'Harmony was deeply wanted and loved.

'He was the bridging of mine and Chris' families (from our previous relationships in which we each have two children) into one and our family deserves compassion and privacy. This was supposed to be our happy ending.'

In a series of photos shared on Instagram on September 7, Ms Negara posed alongside her partner, and her two young children from a previous relationship, as she spoke of their loss.

'Creating life with the love of my life has been the most profound healing journey I could have never imagined being written into our journey,' she wrote in an Instagram post.

'Growing life for nearly ten months, growing our family, falling so deeply in love in a union that was always destined to be, falling in love with the life we have created for our family, birthing life, and then birthing death has been incomprehensible.

'My body feels broken and aches for our baby, the life we grew together. I don't think we will ever know how to move through this heartbreak.

In a series of photos shared on Instagram in September, Ms Negara posed alongside her partner as she spoke of their unfathomable loss

'Our little boy Harmony Hunter due 8.8 born 28 August 2026 at 4.27am in the most powerful birth of our lives, passing peacefully in our arms at 8pm that night.

'Our hearts sit in deep gratitude to our friends who have loved and cared for us this past week, to our community, to Lismore Hospital who worked tirelessly to save Harmony and treat me for postpartum haemorrhage, the NeoRESQ team who flew to Lismore Hospital and continued to spend hours trying to save our little boy, and to Gold Coast University Hospital who held us so deeply as we spent three nights and four days in Comfort Care as a family.'

She also revealed plans to hold a private burial near their home.

'We will soon lay our angel to rest on Bundjalung Country where he was born, the land that has held my family and continues to hold our family. We know you will return to us again old soul, we can feel you surrounding us, our Angel.'

The post was inundated with supportive comments from the influencer's famous friends.

'Oh my darling heart, you Wonder Woman. Loving you both so much,' commented P.E Nation designer Pip Edwards.

'Pal... sending strength your way,' wrote White Fox founder Marty Fox.

Influencer Ruby Tuesday Matthews simply added a white heart emoji, while model Sarah Stephens wrote: 'Oh Pala, I am so sorry.  My heart breaks for you two. Sending all my love.'

The circumstances surrounding Harmony's birth and death have not been publicly established, including why he was born almost three weeks after his due date. (Ms Negara is pictured at Australian Fashion Week in Sydney on May 14, 2024)

Ms Negara appeared on the reality series Ex on the Beach: Couples in 2023

The circumstances surrounding Harmony's birth and death have not been publicly established, including why he was born almost three weeks after his due date.

Friends told the Mail that Negara had chosen home births for both her older children, aged six and eight, while living in Melbourne and was determined to do the same with Harmony.

'Pala is very much about female empowerment,' the friend added.

Ms Negara appeared on the reality series Ex on the Beach: Couples in 2023.

Represented by GIANT Model Management, she has appeared in campaigns for Myer alongside Jennifer Hawkins, Carla Zampatti and Nude by Nature.

WATCH: Police Try to Lasso 'Maggie' the Runaway Highland Cow Who Escaped New York Farm

A four-year-old Highland cow named Maggie who evaded her owners and police for several days in Carmel, New York, was finally captured safely over the weekend.
The post WATCH: Police Try to Lasso ‘Maggie’ the Runaway Highland Cow Who Escaped New York Farm appeared first on Breitbart.

Actual Article Body:
A four-year-old Highland cow named Maggie who evaded her owners and police for several days in Carmel, New York, was finally captured safely over the weekend.

The red-colored cow escaped from Little Cabin’s Farm on Tuesday and decided she did not want to return home for several days, the New York Post reported Sunday.

Numerous Putnam County residents tried to help corral her as she trotted along the edges of roadways, but their attempts to help ultimately failed.

One video taken by a driver showed police officers trying to catch Maggie who bounded away from them. She appeared quite brave as she wove in and out of vehicles stopped on the roadway.

At one point, an individual who appeared to be an officer tried to lasso Maggie who ran in the opposite direction:

The Post article said the lasso attempts eventually helped corral her. She has since been reunited safely with her calf.

The Highland cow, better known in Scotland as the “Highland coo,” is one of the oldest registered breeds of cattle, according to the Highland Cattle Society’s website:

The Highland breed of cattle has a long and distinguished ancestry, not only in its homeland of western Scotland, but also in many far-flung parts of the world. It is one of the oldest registered breeds of cattle in the world and one of Britain’s oldest, most distinctive and best-known breeds.

Written records go back to the 18th century and the Highland Cattle Herd Book, first published in 1885, lists every pedigree since that time. With a long, thick, flowing coat of rich hair and majestic sweeping horns, the Highlander breed has remained largely unchanged over the centuries. Although the classic image of a Highland cow today is red they also come in other shades including yellow, brindle, dun, white and also black, the breed’s original colour.

In a social media post, the farm said “The great Carmel cow adventure has officially come to an end! After days of searching, sleepless nights, and one final cowboy-style chase, Maggie is safely home Little Cabin’s Farm.”

“A HUGE thank you to the police officers and our wonderful community for all the help, love, and support! Once Maggie settles in, she’ll be welcoming visitors! Stay tuned to our social media pages for updates!” the post read.
